purpose: Resolve the counterterror-to-platform lineage and theater-transfer fog by separating institution-level Army intelligence evolution, Palantir's filer-reported product history, exact later Army procurements, and the still-missing technical transfer into ICE. The wave preserves public-system alternatives and refuses to infer a vendor-specific lineage from functional similarity alone.

method.null_hypothesis: public institutions independently developed and procured successive intelligence, identity, targeting, and command systems while commercial vendors entered different programs through ordinary adaptation and competition
method.promotion_rule: An official Army record may establish an institutional lineage, transfer, procurement, or deployment. An SEC filing establishes the registrant's reported company and product history. Neither source type may silently prove the other's proposition, and brand or function continuity may not substitute for technical, contractual, data, personnel, or governance transfer records.
method.transfer_rule: A qualifying transfer requires an exact object, sending-side record, receiving-side record, mechanism, date, changed implementation, and an independent-development comparator.

records.proposition: Palantir was founded to build software for the U.S. intelligence community's counterterrorism work and released Gotham for intelligence-sector customers before expanding the product family into broader government and commercial use.
records.observation: Palantir reports that it was founded in 2003 and began building software for the U.S. intelligence community to assist counterterrorism investigations and operations; released Gotham in 2008 for intelligence customers; later expanded into broader government and commercial functions; and subsequently added Foundry, Apollo, and AIP.
supports: a filer-reported company and product-family origin chronology
a declared counterterrorism-to-broader-government and commercial expansion strategy
an exact acquisition target for independent validation
does_not_support: independent proof of every early deployment or result
a specific intelligence customer or contract
technical continuity into TITAN, NGC2, ICM, or ImmigrationOS
a coordinated founder-network design
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the early intelligence-community contracts, In-Q-Tel or other development instruments where publicly available, Gotham version and deployment records, user and mission records, performance and failure evidence, and exact later product lineage.
records.falsifier: Independent contract and product records materially contradict the reported origin, release, customers, mission use, or claimed expansion chronology.

records.proposition: The Army independently developed and fielded an integrated intelligence platform that moved from wartime quick-reaction use in Iraq and Afghanistan to service-wide deployment.
records.observation: The Army states that DCGS-A had been used extensively as a quick-reaction capability in Iraq and Afghanistan and was approved in December 2012 for full deployment as a globally networked Army intelligence system.
supports: a public-institution platform lineage from expeditionary use to service-wide normalization
P2-to-P3 transition through an Army-led architecture
counterevidence to a claim that a private vendor originated the entire integrated-intelligence trajectory
does_not_support: effective performance in every deployment
absence of commercial components or vendor influence
continuity into later Palantir products
an ordinary or fair option set in every procurement
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the quick-reaction, acquisition, architecture, integrator, data-rights, source-code, user, performance, protest, replacement, and retirement records for each DCGS-A increment and commercial alternative.
records.falsifier: The system was not materially used in the stated theaters, did not transition to service-wide deployment, or depended from inception on the private architecture whose independent origin is under test.

records.proposition: The Army transferred biometric identity-resolution and watchlisting methods developed in Iraq and Afghanistan into enduring and geographically broader intelligence missions.

sources.title: Intelligence center develops Biometrically Enabled Intelligence to support warfighter

records.observation: The Army describes biometric collection, high-confidence identity resolution, fusion with all-source intelligence, watchlist dissemination, employment denial, questioning or targeting support, and operational use in Iraq and Afghanistan. It states that the capability had grown beyond its wartime roots and describes use against other enduring and emerging threats and in the U.S. Pacific Command area.
supports: a bounded two-sided institutional transfer of a method from wartime theaters to broader missions
L2 identity resolution, L3 relationship inference, L5 decision support, L6 effect, and L8 replication
a non-vendor-specific origin and transfer pathway for population and identity intelligence
does_not_support: Palantir involvement
lawfulness or accuracy of every watchlist or decision
transfer into ICE, CBP, or a civilian administrative system
a common private design or extraction cycle
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the biometric systems, vendors, data and watchlist governance, theater versions, transfer orders, receiving-unit records, error and correction history, employment or targeting consequences, and civilian or allied interfaces.
records.falsifier: The broader uses were independently developed, did not reuse the wartime method or data architecture, or the described transfer did not occur operationally.

records.proposition: Palantir's Army role expanded from a commercial alternative challenging DCGS acquisition into later intelligence-targeting and command-and-control platform awards.

sources.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit
sources.title: Palantir USG, Inc. v. United States, Appeal No. 17-1465
Army Tactical Intelligence Targeting Access Node ground station prototype award
Army and industry align on common data baseline, as NGC2 moves from prototyping to delivery

records.observation: The judicial record establishes Palantir's DCGS-A2 commercial-item gate challenge. The Army later selected Palantir after competitive prototyping to deliver TITAN intelligence and targeting ground-station prototypes and identifies Palantir Foundry as an integrated component of the Anduril-led NGC2 edge-to-cloud data mesh.
supports: an actor-specific Army intelligence, targeting, and command-platform expansion sequence
movement from commercial alternative and gate challenge into later competitive prototype and integrated implementation roles
does_not_support: that the DCGS litigation caused TITAN or NGC2 selection
the same source code, ontology, data, or product across all programs
an improperly tailored award
a system-wide founder-network design
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire every intervening solicitation, prototype, evaluation, technical baseline, product and version, contract, user, performance, data and interface right, personnel transition, protest, nonaward, and replacement record.
records.falsifier: The programs use unrelated products and teams, Palantir's role is marginal, or independent requirements and competition fully explain the sequence without durable product or institutional continuity.

records.proposition: The Palantir product family carried a counterterror intelligence pattern—data integration, hidden-pattern identification, analyst-to-operator handoff, and operational feedback—into later reusable government platforms.

sources.title: Army Tactical Intelligence Targeting Access Node ground station prototype award
Army and industry align on common data baseline, as NGC2 moves from prototyping to delivery

records.observation: Palantir's filing describes Gotham as built for counterterror analysts to integrate intelligence, identify hidden patterns, and hand findings to operational users. Later Army records describe Palantir roles in AI-enabled sensor processing and targeting through TITAN and in a Foundry-based edge-to-cloud command data mesh in NGC2.
supports: a functional lineage from counterterror analysis and operational handoff into later intelligence and command platforms
does_not_support: an exact technical transfer
the same codebase, ontology, model, data, or personnel
the absence of independent Army architecture and requirements
transfer into ICE or civilian governance
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire product and version lineage, code and architecture records, ontology and data schemas, contracts, development teams, feature histories, migration documents, Government requirements, and independent-development controls across Gotham, TITAN, Foundry, and NGC2.
records.falsifier: The later systems were independently developed and share only generic data-integration or analytics functions without transferred product, method, personnel, or technical baseline.

records.proposition: The current public record establishes the exact software, code, ontology, model, data, or personnel transferred from counterterror Gotham into TITAN and NGC2.
records.observation: The sources establish company history, product names in some endpoints, functional continuity, Army contracts, and later integrated roles. They do not supply a product-version crosswalk, code or architecture lineage, ontology or model transfer, data migration, personnel transfer, or Government requirement lineage sufficient to identify the exact transferred object.
does_not_support: a completed BRG-01 technical transfer
Gotham as the TITAN product
Gotham as the NGC2 Palantir component
shared code or ontology
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire product bills of materials, versions, code and repository history, architecture, interfaces, ontology, models, data formats, engineering teams, contract requirements, migration, licensing, and Government acceptance records at both endpoints.
records.falsifier: The endpoint records show distinct products, teams, requirements, and architectures with no material transferred object beyond generic commercial capabilities.

records.proposition: Palantir's counterterror platform or method was technically transferred into ICE ICM or ImmigrationOS and materially shaped immigration-enforcement consequences.
records.observation: The current record establishes Palantir's filer-reported counterterror origin, broad functional similarities, ICE ICM and ImmigrationOS procurement and deployment, and designed enforcement workflows. It does not identify the exact counterterror product, feature, ontology, data model, technical baseline, development team, export mechanism, contract requirement, or receiving-system change that moved into ICE.
supports: a narrowed two-endpoint BRG-03 acquisition lane
does_not_support: a technical or organizational transfer from a counterterror theater to ICE
common data or watchlists
Palantir causation of a specific immigration consequence
system-wide normalization
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire both endpoint contracts and architectures, product/version identifiers, feature lineage, data and ontology schemas, engineering and personnel history, requirements authorship, migration records, system interfaces, and consequential case traces.
records.falsifier: The ICE systems were independently developed for distinct legal and operational requirements and contain no transferred counterterror product, method, data, personnel, or technical baseline.

records.proposition: The post-9/11 identity, intelligence integration, watchlisting, targeting, and platform-normalization trajectory originated solely in a founder-controlled private network.

sources.title: Intelligence center develops Biometrically Enabled Intelligence to support warfighter

records.observation: Army records independently document public quick-reaction intelligence systems, service-wide deployment, biometric identity resolution, all-source fusion, watchlisting, decision support, effects, and transfer beyond wartime roots. These public programs preclude treating the entire architecture as having a solely private-network origin.
supports: a strong public-institution origin and co-development alternative
continued testing of later private control over particular components and gates
does_not_support: absence of private market shaping or vendor dependence
effective public control in every later system
no founder-network role in selected programs
a complete public capacity and rights ledger
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Build the complete public and private capability, authorship, funding, personnel, integrator, rights, and successor ledger across each phase and program.
records.falsifier: Operative records show the nominally public programs were designed, controlled, and reproduced by the same private network from inception.

records.proposition: The combined institutional and Palantir lineage records establish that one founder-controlled network converted the full counterterror architecture into a coordinated transnational population-governance system.
records.observation: Wave 06 establishes an Army institutional lineage, a biometric-method transfer, Palantir's filer-reported counterterror origin, an actor-specific Army platform expansion, and functional continuity into TITAN and NGC2. It also preserves independent public architectures and lacks exact transfer into ICE, common governance, cross-entity planning, civilian consequence chains, and causal private benefit.
supports: continued testing of bounded platform, method, and theater transfers
does_not_support: system-wide counterterror-origin capture
one founder-controlled transnational organism
common design across companies, funds, banks, policy organizations, and agencies
coercive civilian governance or extraction
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Require exact cross-program transfer objects, common governance or planning, public-versus-private rights persistence, two-sided civilian transfers, consequential case chains, and causal residual-benefit ledgers.
records.falsifier: Complete program and actor denominators show independent public development, ordinary vendor adaptation, distinct products, effective competition and exit, and no common private governance or transfer architecture.
